content.title: About
content.content: Almonds, chocolate covered candy are almonds coated in chocolate, made from the edible seeds of the almond tree (Prunus dulcis). Almonds have a mild, slightly sweet, nutty flavor and a crunchy texture, while the chocolate coating adds sweetness and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almonds are related to peaches, plums, and cherries; the almond itself is the seed inside the fruit's pit.
Sweet almonds are the ones eaten as food; bitter almonds contain toxic compounds and are not sold as ordinary snacks.
Almond trees have been cultivated for thousands of years.
Almonds are used to make almond flour, almond butter, marzipan, and almond milk.
Almond blossoms appear in early spring, before the leaves.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Almonds are one of the best food sources of vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant that protects cells.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Almonds contain mostly monounsaturated fats, which are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Almonds contribute plant protein and dietary fiber, promoting fullness.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Almonds contain more calcium than most other nuts.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Almonds can cause allergic reactions, which may be severe in some people.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Almonds are calorie‑dense, so portions should be moderate.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole almonds are not suitable for young children because they can cause choking.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Almonds contain oxalates; people prone to kidney stones may need to limit intake. Bitter almonds should never be eaten raw.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chocolate‑covered almonds can be enjoyed as a snack, added to granola, yogurt, baked goods, or desserts. The chocolate coating makes them especially popular in festive sweets.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chocolate‑covered almonds in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent oil rancidity. Discard any that smell rancid, sharp, or stale.

content.title: About
content.content: Salted dry cottage cheese is a dehydrated curd product made from skimmed milk. It has a firm texture, a pronounced salty taste, and is used both as a snack and as an ingredient in various dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dry cottage cheese is a staple in many Eastern European cuisines.
Its lower moisture content gives it a longer shelf life than fresh cottage cheese.
It can be produced from cow, goat, or sheep milk.
Often used as a filling for dumplings, pierogies, and pastries.
In some regions it is referred to as “curd cheese.”

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Provides high‑quality milk protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The skimmed version contains little fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Digestive friendliness
items.content: Reduced lactose content makes it easier to digest for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Excessive intake of salted curd can contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Sodium considerations
items.content: People monitoring sodium intake should limit portion sizes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy it as a snack, crumble it into salads, use as a filling for baked goods, dumplings, or pancakes. It can also be grated over dishes for added texture and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, it remains good for 2–3 weeks. Discard if it develops a sour odor or off‑color.

content.title: About
content.content: Jelly is a semi‑solid dessert made by gelling fruit or berry juice with a gelling agent, usually gelatin, agar‑agar or pectin. It has a soft, slightly springy texture and a sweet flavor that depends on the ingredients used.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The earliest references to jelly date back to ancient Rome, where fish gelatin was used.
Modern fruit jelly appeared in the 19th century after gelatin became mass‑produced.
Jelly is popular in culinary shows because it can be molded into any shape and color.
Agar‑agar, derived from seaweed, allows vegetarian jelly without animal gelatin.
Pectin, naturally found in apples and citrus, gels when combined with sugar and acid.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Jelly made with minimal added sugar provides a light dessert with few calories.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: The fruit juice base retains vitamin C, which supports the immune system.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Jelly is mostly water, helping to maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Its soft texture is quickly digested and suitable for people with chewing difficulties.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Depending on the fruit used, jelly can provide potassium, magnesium, and small amounts of iron.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Traditional jelly often contains high amounts of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and tooth decay.

items.title: Gelatin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to animal gelatin.

items.title: Artificial additives
items.content: Commercial jelly may contain artificial colors and flavors that can cause sensitivities.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Excessive consumption can cause stomach upset due to high sugar and acidity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve jelly chilled as a standalone dessert, layer it in cakes, use it as a filling for pastries, or add it to fruit salads. It can be cut into cubes, molded into shapes, or served in glasses with fresh berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep jelly in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze it in portion‑sized molds to preserve texture and flavor.
